Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testGetTypeArguments()` is failing, specifically the part that verifies the mapping of type variables for partially-assigned classes. It expects to find 2 type arguments for `Other.class` when considered as a subclass of `This.class`, but the method `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class)` returns a map that does not match this expectation.

Inspecting the method `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>)`, it delegates to an overloaded private method that handles different types of `Type`: `Class`, `ParameterizedType`, `GenericArrayType`, `WildcardType`, and `TypeVariable`.

For `Class<?>` types, the method `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)` performs these steps:
- Checks if `cls` is assignable to `toClass`.
- Handles primitive types by wrapping them.
- Copies incoming type variable assignments.
- Checks if the target class has been reached by verifying if `cls` has any type parameters or if `toClass.equals(cls)`. If true, it returns the type variable assignment map immediately (line 675: `if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls)) { return typeVarAssigns; }`).
- Otherwise, it recursively walks to the closest parent type and continues.

This conditional at line 675 is likely the root cause of the issue. The check `cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0` is used to determine if the type parameters are available at the current class, but when we have a partially-assigned class scenario (where some type variables may be assigned and some are inherited), this condition may cause an early return, missing the discovery or merging of type arguments from parent classes/interfaces.

Since partially-assigned type arguments often arise in cases where a class is parameterized and it extends or implements another parameterized class/interface with some type arguments already fixed, returning early here will result in missing type arguments for the `toClass`.

Other code paths for `ParameterizedType` and the recursive use of the method `getClosestParentType` seem to correctly continue collecting type arguments through the hierarchy, but this crucial conditional in the `Class<?>` handler leads to incomplete type argument accumulation.

Thus, the bug is an early return in the `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)` method when the current class has type parameters, causing incomplete type argument maps and failing the test case that expects all relevant type arguments to be present for partially-assigned classes.

Relevant issue from the bug report text:
The bug report states the test failure is due to `TypeUtils.getTypeArguments()` missing type arguments in partially-assigned classes, which matches exactly this early return issue.

No other recent bug reports are relevant.

Summary:
The root cause is the condition `if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls))` in `getTypeArguments(Class<?>, Class<?>, Map)` causes the method to prematurely return without correctly resolving or merging type arguments from superclasses/interfaces, leading to incomplete type argument maps for partially-assigned generic classes.

This explains the failing test case that expects 2 type arguments but receives fewer or incomplete mappings.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
